item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00415","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C16","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 is a clear material drafting template for the child. Both are short presidential letters responding to a congressional chamber's resolution about the same displaced Greek children. They use closely corresponding language to describe thousands of children removed from Greece to eastern Europe, affirm shared humanitarian concern, cite United Nations efforts, promise continued Executive Branch action, and call for the children's return to their parents and homeland. C16 shares the Greek-conflict setting but not this specific drafting machinery; C23 has a humanitarian and United Nations appeal but lacks the distinctive subject and structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I know that all Americans share the Senate's humanitarian concern for the thousands of Greek children removed from Greece during the guerrilla warfare and now being held in eastern Europe.","parent_excerpt":"I fully share the concern of the House of Representatives for the thousands of children removed from Greece to eastern Europe by the communist guerrilla forces","explanation":"Distinctive near-parallel opening adapted from the House and its resolution to the Senate and its resolution."},{"child_excerpt":"the unjustified retention of these innocent children far from their parents and their native land","parent_excerpt":"calling for the speedy return of these children to their homes and homeland...the reunion of these children with their parents","explanation":"Both frame the same objective through the children's return to their parents and homeland."},{"child_excerpt":"The Executive Branch has exerted and will continue to exert every feasible effort to encourage the repatriation of these children.","parent_excerpt":"The Executive Branch of the Government has been persistent in its endeavors to secure effective compliance with the United Nations resolutions in this case. These efforts will not be relaxed until the Greek children are back in their homes.","explanation":"The child closely reproduces the earlier pledge of persistent and continuing Executive Branch action."},{"child_excerpt":"I am certain that the United Nations has been encouraged in its efforts to effect the children's return by the Senate's deep and sympathetic concern as expressed in S. Res. 212","parent_excerpt":"I welcome the adoption of House Resolution 514...The Executive Branch of the Government has been persistent in its endeavors to secure effective compliance with the United Nations resolutions in this case.","explanation":"Both connect a chamber's resolution with United Nations efforts concerning the children's return."}]}
